punchline: A plane is off course much of its flight and still lands where it should, because it never stops correcting.
thirty_sec: Jack Canfield compares chasing a goal to flying a plane. The plane is off course much of the time, but its instruments keep saying so, and it keeps correcting until it lands. His advice is to get your own readings. Ask someone to rate your work together from 1 to 10, then ask what it would take to make it a 10. A miss becomes a correction, not a verdict.
question: What's the most useful criticism you've ever received, and did you have to ask for it?
